primary_meaning: Jesus Christ himself as the personal source, embodiment, and giver of spiritual/eternal life (zoe)
primary_basis: John 14:6 ('I am the way, and the truth, and the life')
John 11:25 ('I am the resurrection and the life')
1 John 1:1–2 ('the Word of life… the life was made manifest')

alternatives.meaning: Eternal life as the gift/state of salvation and communion with God granted to believers
Physical/biological life (nephesh/psyche) as the created animating principle given by God
The Holy Spirit as the life-giving presence and power
The Tree of Life as eschatological symbol of immortality and restored paradise

notes: In New Testament usage and historic Christian teaching the definite form 'the life' most consistently functions as a christological title or as the divine/eternal life that is identical with or flows from Christ; physical life and the Tree of Life remain important but secondary symbolic registers. The distinction between zoe (divine life) and bios/psyche (creaturely life) is widely recognized in biblical studies.
